sec.footnote: Signature-based detection on nginx URLs & User-Agents, so false positives/negatives are possible. Request bodies (POST) are not logged and not inspected. A 2xx response on an attack URL is usually the SPA fallback (index.html); compare its size with a normal page.
sec.footnote_crs: Detection uses the OWASP Core Rule Set {version} (Apache 2.0 licence) at paranoia level {pl}: {n} rules; a request counts as an attack when its anomaly score is ≥ {th}. Categories follow the MITRE CAPEC catalogue. Only the parts of the request recorded in the nginx log are checked (URL, query arguments, User-Agent); POST bodies, cookies and other headers are not logged, so this is not a WAF replacement and can still produce false positives/negatives. A 2xx response on an attack URL is usually the SPA fallback (index.html); compare the response size with a normal page.

home.title_a: Watch your service logs, security and servers
home.lead: MoniShield reads logs from S3, Kafka or a collector on your servers, detects attacks with OWASP CRS rules, shows the CPU, memory and disk of servers and containers, finds the cause of errors and sends a daily report to Telegram, Discord or email.
home.live.title: Where Requests Come from
home.live.intro: Request origins over the last minute, refreshed every few seconds. Each dot stands for an area of about 50 km and holds no IP address.
home.day.intro: Request origins in the logs of {d}. Each dot stands for an area of about 50 km and holds no IP address.
home.sample.intro: There is no traffic to show yet, so this map uses sample data. Real dots appear as soon as requests come in.
home.f.title: Main Features
home.f.intro: See service health, attacks, server load and the causes of errors without opening log files one by one.
home.f.1.d: Log lines, HTTP requests, errors and the 5xx rate per day, compared with the average of the last 7 days. The status of the day shows at once: safe, needs a look or critical.
home.f.2.d: Requests are matched with OWASP CRS rules and grouped by CAPEC category, such as SQL injection, path traversal and scanners. Every attacking IP has a profile page and shows on the map.
home.f.3.d: Errors are grouped by service and by pattern, such as repeated 401s, expired tokens, upstream connection problems and DNS. A service whose errors jump is flagged.
home.f.4.d: CPU, memory, disk and network of every server and Docker container, every 30 seconds. A value far above its usual level for that hour is flagged, with a link to the logs of that container.
home.how.title: How It Works
home.priv.title: Privacy and Security
home.priv.d: Log data stays on your server. Only summary numbers are sent out.
cf.pub.intro: The home page (/) can be opened by anyone without signing in. Its map shows request origins rounded to ±50 km areas; areas with fewer than 3 requests are hidden and there are no IP addresses.
cf.pub.map: Show the traffic map on the home page
home.how.intro: How data flows from incoming logs and metrics to reports. Everything runs on your server.
home.arch.label: MoniShield Architecture Diagram
home.arch.1.a: Object storage: Amazon S3, S3-compatible and Azure Blob
home.arch.1.b: Kafka for realtime logs from the cluster
home.arch.1.c: Collector (OpenTelemetry) on Linux, Windows, Docker and Kubernetes
home.arch.2.a: Log formats per service: nginx, Caddy, Spring Boot, JSON, logfmt, syslog
home.arch.2.b: Attack detection with OWASP CRS and CAPEC
home.arch.2.c: IP owner and location from offline databases
home.arch.3.a: DuckDB per source: S3, Kafka and collector
home.arch.3.b: Server metrics: 30-second points for 7 days, hourly values for 90 days
home.arch.3.c: PostgreSQL for accounts, roles and the audit log
home.arch.4.a: Versioned API (/api/v1) with sessions, roles and encrypted payloads
home.arch.4.b: Svelte dashboard in two languages, dark and light themes
home.arch.4.c: Telegram, Discord and email notifications, and a live map
home.arch.layers.d: Business rules do not depend on any framework. The dependency direction between layers is checked by automated tests.
home.arch.deploy.d: Runs with Docker Compose behind Caddy (automatic HTTPS). Every change goes through CI on GitHub Actions: Python tests, the UI build, a browser test of every page and a check of the Caddy configuration, before it is deployed automatically.
home.priv.1.d: IP addresses are never sent to third-party services, including the map on this page.
home.priv.2.d: IP owner and location come from databases downloaded to the server.
home.priv.3.d: Telegram, Discord and email messages hold summary numbers and a link to the dashboard only.
home.priv.4.d: The dashboard opens only with an admin or user account, and API data is sent encrypted.
home.end.title: Already Have an Account?
home.end.d: Sign in to open the dashboard. Accounts are created by an admin.

raw.intro: Search the original lines of every service in this date's log files: words, a regular expression, a request ID or an IP. Lines are shown exactly as the services wrote them. Every search and download is recorded in the audit log.

lf.intro: How MoniShield reads the lines of each service. A wrong format means no errors, levels or map for that service.
lf.saved_done: Rules saved and in use. New lines are read with them now, no restart needed. Lines that came in earlier keep their old reading.
lf.read_toast: Reading today's folder again with the new rules.
lf.empty_text: Services appear here once logs of the last 7 days are read.
lf.read_na_tip: Unread lines are not counted for this built-in format.
lf.table_hint: Changing a format here writes a rule for that service on that host only. Services you do not change keep their current reading. A suggestion comes from trying every format on the last 200 lines.
lf.rules_intro: Rules are checked from top to bottom; the first one whose name fits the service is used. The last rule catches every other service.
lf.comments_note: Saving rewrites log-formats.toml. Comments written by hand in the file are not kept.
lf.builtin_note: These are the built-in rules. Saving writes them to log-formats.toml, and only then do they come from the file.
lf.test_text: Format {f}. Showing the last {n} entries of {day}.
lf.test_none_text: No log lines of this service were found in the last 7 days.
lf.test_ok_text: Every line is read: time, level and, for access logs, IP, method, path and status.
lf.test_bad_text: {bad} of {n} lines are not read, so errors and levels stay at 0 for them. Try the suggested format.
lf.err_name: This service name cannot be written in a rule.
lf.err_match: Enter a service name or a glob for the rule.
lf.err_lines: Line {n} must look like name = value.
lf.f_hint.match: A service name or a glob such as web-*, optionally with a namespace: shop/web-*.
lf.f_hint.fields: One per line: column = key in the log. A dotted key reaches inside nested JSON.
lf.f_hint.pattern: A regular expression with named groups. It needs time and message; level, ip, method, path and status are optional.
lf.f_hint.time_format: iso, epoch, epoch_ms, clf or a strptime pattern such as %d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%S.
lf.f_hint.multiline: A regular expression that marks the first line of an entry; other lines join the entry above them.
lf.f_hint.levels: One per line: the site's word = ERROR, WARN, INFO or DEBUG.
lf.f_hint.ip_header: The field that holds the client address behind a proxy.
lf.f_hint.duration_unit: The unit of the mapped duration; it is stored as milliseconds.

home.f.5.d: Search the original log lines of every service at once, and follow one request across all services by its request ID.
home.f.6.d: Alerts to Telegram, Discord or email on a spike, a critical attack, a failed ingest or a log folder that has not arrived. The daily report goes out at the hour you set.
home.col.title: Connect a Server in Two Commands
home.col.intro: A small collector (OpenTelemetry) runs on each server and sends logs and metrics to MoniShield over HTTPS. Add it on the Collectors page, copy the commands, and the first lines arrive within a minute.
home.col.note.linux: Ubuntu, Debian, RHEL, Rocky and other systemd Linux, amd64 or arm64.
home.col.note.docker: Runs on the Docker host and names each log after its container.
home.col.note.windows: Windows Server 2016 or newer; reads files and the Windows Event Log.
home.col.note.kubernetes: The official Helm chart; the key step and the values file come from the Collectors page.
home.col.1.d: On the Collectors page, give the server a name and a group, and choose its logs and metrics.
home.col.2.d: Copy the two commands to the server. The token works once, for 24 hours.
home.col.3.d: The collector shows Online, logs appear under Raw Logs and the server appears on the Servers page.
home.col.fact.1: Sends over HTTPS; no port opened on the server
home.col.fact.2: Its own key per server, replaced or revoked at any time
home.col.fact.3: Keeps data in a queue while the line is down
home.col.fact.4: Upgrades in place with one command
home.arch.1.d: Log folder upload in the browser
home.arch.3.d: Daily backup, can be copied to object storage
home.priv.5.t: Collector over HTTPS with Its Own Key
home.priv.5.d: Each server sends with its own key; the receiver lives on a separate host that serves nothing else.
home.priv.6.d: Metrics hold numbers only: no command lines, environment values or IP addresses.
home.pv.label_sv: Example of the MoniShield Servers page with sample data: an unusual-value banner, servers by group with CPU, memory and disk, and CPU and memory charts.
home.gs.title: Getting Started
home.gs.intro: From the first sign-in to a daily report in five steps. Every setting is made in the dashboard; no configuration file needs editing.
home.gs.1.short: An admin creates your account; change the first password.
home.gs.1.i1: Open the dashboard and sign in with the account the admin gave you.
home.gs.1.i2: Choose a new password on the first sign-in (at least 12 characters).
home.gs.1.i3: Pick the language and the theme in the header; both are remembered.
home.gs.1.i4: Admins add more people under the user menu → Manage Users, as admin or user.
home.gs.2.short: S3 bucket, Kafka topic or a collector on each server.
home.gs.2.i1: Object storage: give the bucket and an access key (read-only is enough); new daily folders are read on their own.
home.gs.2.i2: Kafka: give the brokers and the topic for logs that arrive in real time.
home.gs.2.i3: Collector: Add Collector, copy the two commands to the server, and its logs and metrics arrive within a minute.
home.gs.2.i4: Switch between S3, Kafka and Collector with the Data Source switch in the header.
home.gs.3.short: Make sure every service is read the right way.
home.gs.3.i1: Open Log Formats and turn on Only Services That Read Badly.
home.gs.3.i2: Use Test Lines to see how the last lines of a service are read.
home.gs.3.i3: Pick the suggested format (for example caddy-json or plain) for the service and press Save Rules.
home.gs.3.i4: Press Read Today Again so the lines of today are read with the new rule.
home.gs.4.short: Start at the Overview, then follow what needs a look.
home.gs.4.i1: Overview: the status of the day (safe, needs a look or critical) against the 7-day average.
home.gs.4.i2: Security: attacking IPs, attack categories and failed logins; every IP has a profile page.
home.gs.4.i3: Root Causes: errors grouped by service and pattern, with the lines behind them in Raw Logs.
home.gs.4.i4: Servers: CPU, memory and disk of every server and container, with unusual values flagged.
home.gs.5.short: Telegram, Discord or email, and a daily report.
home.gs.5.i1: Fill in Telegram, Discord or email and press Send Test.
home.gs.5.i2: Choose the events for each channel: Spike, Critical Attack, Ingest Failed, Log Folder Missing and more.
home.gs.5.i3: Set the Daily Report Hour; the report holds numbers and a link only.
home.gs.5.i4: Set Spike Thresholds per service so a busy service does not alert all day.
